daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The Constitutional Court ruled that Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka does not meet the educational requirements for his position, sparking widespread political debate. The Court found that Gibran's undergraduate diploma cannot be verified, though the Presidential Palace insisted the diploma exists but has not been found. The ruling has prompted discussion about potential MPR action, while President Prabowo's political direction after the MK decision is being closely watched.

  • Golkar Party announced Prabowo as its 2029 presidential candidate but left the vice presidential slot open, indicating Gibran remains a possibility.
  • The DPR is revising the Election Law with discussions covering additional parliamentary seats and e-accounting measures.
  • President Prabowo expressed surprise at the enthusiastic reception for Sherly Tjoanda, noting that elections are still far off.
  • Vice President Gibran continued receiving visitors at the Vice Presidential Palace, saying he is focused on his work.
  • Gibran addressed a pastors' congress, stressing religious freedom and tolerance.
  • Pratikno defended the size of the Presidential Advisory Council, saying it will make advice more comprehensive despite criticism that it is bloated.
  • Deputy Vice President Muhaimin Iskandar called for a shift to empowerment in poverty alleviation strategies.

Foreign Policy & Defence

China officially welcomed Arrmanatha Nasir as Indonesia's new Foreign Minister, with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi extending congratulations on his appointment. The diplomatic recognition marks the formal start of bilateral engagement under Indonesia's new cabinet. Meanwhile, Indonesia successfully championed a resolution on child nutrition access at the UN Human Rights Council.

  • Indonesian immigration authorities deported a Thai fugitive wanted in a corruption case after detection by immigration systems.
  • The Navy's strategic acquisition of KRI Sriwijaya-100 is being analyzed for next operational steps.

Other

The Indonesia Stock Exchange announced stricter IPO requirements, eliminating minimum share price thresholds while tightening listing criteria for companies. The move aims to improve market quality as the Jakarta Composite Index opened weak, nearly falling below the 6,000 level. The regulatory change follows broader market volatility affecting Indonesian equities.

  • The government confirmed mandatory halal certification will take effect on 18 October as scheduled.
  • Gojek responded to the new presidential regulation on ride-hailing, stating GoRide commissions have been 8 percent since July.
  • State holding company Danantara instructed INKA to transform to meet rail demand in Indonesia.
  • Indonesia is planning thousands of health facility upgrades from 2027-2029.
  • The Education Minister announced that students will not automatically advance in 2027, ending the "rajin-malas sama saja" (diligent and lazy are the same) situation.
  • The Education Ministry is investigating the bullying death of an elementary school student in Pemalang.
  • Police named four suspects in the Virgo Transport ferry sinking.
